clue.text: Sort of lunch a peer provided for a shoemaker

indicators.note: a 'sort of' lunch is a version of it, so the letters of lunch, a and peer are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman lays on a meal of some kind for the local cobbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' is the anagram signal, working on LUNCH A PEER; 'provided for' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this little fairy is a cobbler, forever mending a single brogue.

clue.text: Sued small company, perhaps, for cash in Lisbon

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: Co. is the short form of company

explanation.surface: Took a little firm to court, maybe, for money in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'small' marks the company as abbreviated. The escudo was Portugal's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Portuguese monetary unit, the money once spent in its capital.

clue.text: Bit of a downfall for a fashionable doctor involved in royal operation

indicators.note: the middle pieces are wrapped inside the outer letters

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy physician caught up in a royal surgery suffers a minor downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin, but here it is a fall of rain; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of rain is one small part of a shower.

clue.text: Fur sported by Greek character upset everyone around island

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes around the island word

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word everyone upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A fur coat is worn by a Greek who has upset everyone on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses ALL to LLA. INCH, a small island, appears in Scottish place names like Inchcolm. 'Sported by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent is a prized fur.

clue.text: A nincompoop swallowing new port

parts.note: a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool gulping down a fresh glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink being swallowed, but it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Belgian city on the Scheldt is one of Europe's busiest seaports.

clue.text: Parsimonious approach

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning come close to

explanation.definitionFit: Close with money means mean; and to draw nigh is to come up to something.

clue.text: At this rate, we'll be able to swap currencies!

definitions.text: At this rate, we'll be able to swap currencies!

parts.words: At this rate, we'll be able to swap currencies!
parts.note: 'At this rate' sounds like an exasperated remark, but read literally it names the rate at which one money is traded for another

explanation.definitionFit: Swapping one thing for another is a trade, and the rate of trading currencies carries this name.

clue.text: Cassandra's supporters? He set out to divide them

indicators.note: the rearranged letters split the supporters word in two

parts.note: props are supports

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of he set are rearranged

explanation.surface: He set out to split the backers of a Trojan princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Cassandra's stands for 'is'. 'Out' rearranges HE SET to HETES, which 'to divide' puts inside PROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra, Priam's daughter, was a seer whose true predictions nobody believed.

clue.text: Priest, an unknown one, has sovereign remedy

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
x is the classic unknown quantity in algebra
I is the Roman numeral for one
R stands for Rex or Regina, the reigning king or queen

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a nameless companion own a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign remedy' reads as one phrase meaning a cure-all, but 'sovereign' gives only R, leaving 'remedy' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist's potion thought to cure every ailment, so a medicine or cure.

clue.text: Militant sees beginning of play and most of "Panorama"

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a stage play

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter here

parts.note: a vista is a wide view, a panorama

explanation.surface: A protester watches the opening of a drama and a large part of a TV current affairs show.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is also a long-running BBC current affairs programme, which the quotation marks play on; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner who takes vigorous action for a cause can be called a militant.

clue.text: Protection provided by many in an armed vessel

indicators.note: the letter for many goes inside the vessel word, as 'in' says

parts.note: a warship is an armed naval vessel
D is the Roman numeral for 500, taken as 'many'

explanation.surface: A crowd aboard a battleship offers security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' as D (500) is an old crossword convention; 'provided by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardianship of a minor by the court, which is a form of protection or custody.

clue.text: Tract where gold is found after a short time

indicators.note: gold is placed after the short time, coming second in the word

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief while
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An area where prospectors strike gold quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse of open upland is a tract of land.

clue.text: Workers accept support and make for the town

indicators.note: the workers take in the support word

parts.note: men are workers, hands
aid means support
to head for a place is to make for it

explanation.surface: Employees agree to back the plan and set off for town.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town on the Thames in Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thames-side town in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: Mineral compound occurring in parts of Rhone

indicators.note: the compound word is found inside the rearranged river name
Rhone is broken into parts and reassembled, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: a blend is a mixture, a compound

explanation.surface: A mineral compound found in certain areas along a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of' is an unusual anagram signal: the river name is broken up and reassembled as HORNE before 'occurring in' places the compound inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark rock-forming silicate, one of the amphibole minerals.

clue.text: Soldiers in assault after brigadier's initial aberration

indicators.note: the soldiers in assault come after the brigadier's letter
the first letter of brigadier's is taken

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to storm is to attack, an assault

explanation.surface: Troops joining an attack after their commander's first move is a sudden lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers in assault' tempts a container, but 'in' stays as its own two letters in the chain, and 'after' puts the brigadier's letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mental lapse or fit of madness is an aberration.

clue.text: Awkwardly takes exercise in popular part of Cambs

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the exercise letters sit inside the town name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily works out in a well-liked corner of Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambs is short for Cambridgeshire, an English county; ELY is a small city in it. 'Takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something clumsily or without skill is acting awkwardly.

clue.text: Scanty team go around university in eastern States

indicators.note: the team-and-go piece sits inside eastern plus States

parts.note: US is the United States
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: the word go goes around the letter for university

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small side heads around a college in the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: XI for a team of eleven is a cricket and football convention; 'around' makes GUO and 'in' sets the team piece inside the eastern States.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiguous is a formal word for meagre or very small in amount.

clue.text: Disorder came with the knife

indicators.note: disorder signals that the letters of came and the are jumbled

explanation.surface: Chaos arrived along with the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting through undergrowth is a type of knife.

clue.text: Sir Rowland did battle, some say, at this stronghold

parts.note: Sir Rowland Hill introduced the Penny Post in Victorian Britain

indicators.note: the word for did battle is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: fought means did battle

explanation.surface: A Victorian postal reformer fought here, according to some, at this fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowland Hill reformed the British postal service in 1840, inventing the postage stamp. 'At this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient fortified hilltop enclosure, such as an Iron Age camp, is a stronghold.

clue.text: Tender nail — new one appearing

parts.note: a pin is a slender nail
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A sore fingernail, with a new one starting to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective about a sore nail; it is a noun, a boat that serves a larger ship. 'Appearing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small boat carried by or attending a larger ship is a ship's tender.

clue.text: Moving abroad, English fighter meets leading seaman coming back

parts.note: a MiG is a Soviet fighter plane

indicators.note: the leading-seaman pieces are read backwards, as if returning

parts.note: No. 1 means first or leading, written NO I
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: An emigrant English pilot meets a senior sailor on the return voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' reverses NO I + TAR to give RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's own country to settle in another is relocating overseas.

clue.text: Man's device for correcting vision

definitions.meaning: belonging to Len, a common male first name
a curved piece of glass in spectacles that bends light

explanation.definitionFit: Len is a man's name, so its possessive fits 'Man's'; and glasses use shaped glass to correct eyesight.

clue.text: Countryman having tea, we hear, in simple surroundings

indicators.note: the drink's letter goes inside the word for simple, which forms the surroundings

parts.note: naive means simple, unsophisticated

indicators.note: the drink is heard as the name of a letter

parts.note: said aloud, tea is the letter T

explanation.surface: A rustic drinks a cuppa in humble surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surroundings' completes the container: NAIVE is around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in a particular country is one of its native people, a fellow countryman.

clue.text: Doctor's husband has employment in the sultanate

indicators.note: the employment word goes inside the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate in Arabia
use means employment, application

explanation.surface: A medic's spouse finds work in an Arabian sultanate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Doctor's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay. A British houseman is a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a junior hospital physician in training is called by this title.

clue.text: Graduate's introduction to Secret Service

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts graduate; the 's adds the letter S

indicators.note: the first letter of Secret is taken

explanation.surface: A new graduate's first step into the Secret Service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret Service' reads as one phrase, but 'Service' is the definition, a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist celebrated in a Catholic church is a religious service.

clue.text: A game a soldier took part in, in the defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier played in a polo match, in which he was a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: The second A follows the soldier in the answer; 'took part in' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written justification of one's beliefs or conduct is a defence.

clue.text: Euterpe's, perhaps, gives rise to merriment

definitions.meaning: belonging to one of the nine Muses, of whom Euterpe, Muse of music, is an example

explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is one of the nine goddesses, so something of hers belongs to one of them; and to entertain is to cause laughter.

clue.text: In print, her witty saying introduced Mrs Henry Dashwood, for one

indicators.note: the witty saying is introduced into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a step can mean a footprint, the print a foot leaves
a mot is a witty remark, a bon mot

explanation.surface: In a book, her clever remark brought a character from Jane Austen into play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Austen's Sense and Sensibility, Mrs Henry Dashwood is the second wife of Henry Dashwood, so stepmother to his son John. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the second wife of John Dashwood's father, so a parent by marriage to him.
